verses.1: And the messengers went to Shaul, the king. They said, “David is hidden in the cave of the rock, on the other side of the Jebus.”
verses.2: Shaul got up and went down to the shore of Ziph. With him were three thousand men from Israel, who came to seek David on the shore of Ziph.
verses.3: And Shaul stood in the valley of the wheat fields, which were located on the banks of the river. David sat by the sea. He saw that Shaul had arrived after him.
verses.4: And David sent messengers, and he knew that Saul had come to Nahum.
verses.5: David stood up and went to the place where Saul was buried. David saw the place where Saul lay buried. Abner, son of Ner, was the commander of the army; and Saul lay on the cross. The people gathered around him.
verses.6: And David said to Ahimelech, “And to Abishai, son of Zeruiah. My brother Joab said, ‘Who will go with me to Shaul at the camp?’ And Abishai said, ‘I will go with you.’”
verses.7: And David and Abishai went to the people at night. There they saw Saul lying asleep in his tent. His tent was spread out on the ground, with Abner and the people lying around him.
verses.8: And Abishai said to David, “Today, God has closed your eyes. Now, let us go into the city once more. I will not leave him again.”
verses.9: And David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him. For whoever reaches out his hand against the anointed one of Jehovah will be punished.”
verses.10: And David said, “May the LORD be with us! If the LORD does not help us, then he will come and die in battle.”
verses.11: May God prevent me from using my hands in the service of Jehovah. Now, please take this staff that is at its tip, and also the paddle for swimming. Let’s go!
verses.12: And David took the chariot and the boat from the beginning of Shaul’s reign. They went there together. But no one can see or know what happened. Everything became dark because the Lord’s death fell upon them.
verses.13: And David went on his way, standing on the top of the mountain, far away from them.
verses.14: And David called to the people and to Abner, son of Ner. He said, “Do not refuse, Abner.” But Abner refused. He said, “Who are you, that you call upon the king?”
verses.15: And David said to Abner, “Do not be afraid! Who is like you in Israel? Why didn’t you keep your king safe from those who wanted to destroy him?”
verses.16: This is not a good thing that you have done, O Jehovah. You are children of death; you have not kept yourself safe from your own gods and from the Messiah of Jehovah. Now, see what has been done by the king’s army and by those who rule over the waters.
verses.17: Shaul recognized David’s voice. He said, “This is the voice of David’s son.” David replied, “My voice is that of the king.”
verses.18: And he said, “Why does this servant of mine keep pursuing his master? What have I done, and what is my fault?”
verses.19: And now, please listen to the words of your servant. If Jehovah has chosen you for this holy day of celebration, and if the people are wicked before Jehovah’s eyes, as if they have taken me away from the inheritance of Jehovah, saying, “You must serve other gods.”
verses.20: And now, let not my image fall to the ground before the face of Yahweh. For it seems that the king of Israel went out to seek a curse from Yahweh, as the scribe was on Mount Sinai.
verses.21: And Shaul said, “I have sinned again, son of David. It did not happen to you before, when my soul was dear to your eyes today. Now I have sinned, and I will pay a heavy price for it.”
verses.22: And David said, “Look, here is the king’s concubine. Let one of the boys go and take her away.”
verses.23: And Jehovah will restore to the man his justice and his truthfulness, which You have given him today. I will not use my hands against Him, for Jehovah has given me this power.
verses.24: And now, as your spirit has grown in my eyes today, so too will my spirit grow in the eyes of Jehovah. And He will save me from all troubles.
verses.25: And Shaul said to David, “Blessed be you, son of David! You will do what I command you. And you will be able to do whatever I ask you.” Then David went on his way, and Shaul returned to his own place.
